title: NACHA WEB Debit Account Validation and the Credit-Push Fraud Vector: The Rule the ODFI Signs, the RDFI Reads, and the AI Verification Layer That Actually Reduces Return Rates
summary: The NACHA Operating Rules for WEB debit entries require a commercially reasonable fraudulent-transaction detection system that validates the receiving account is a legitimate open account before the first ACH debit. Credit-push fraud, which bypasses the WEB rule entirely by tricking the sender into originating a legitimate ACH credit, is the fastest-growing ACH fraud vector. The rule mechanics, the account-validation architecture we run, and the counter-controls on the credit-push side of the ledger.
